LAREDO — Five names are on the ballot for mayor of Laredo on November 3. Four of them have shown voters their money. The fifth, Jorge A. Garza, has nothing on file for the public to see.

Under Title 15 of the Texas Election Code, every candidate files campaign finance reports with the City Secretary's Office, and the city posts them on its Campaign Finance Reports page. The most important of those reports before Election Day is the 30th-day report — for this election, due Monday, October 5, 2026, covering all campaign activity from July 1 through September 24, 2026. It is the last full look voters get at who is financing each campaign before early voting begins.

What the city's page shows

Under the October 5, 2026 deadline, the city's Mayor list links to a filed report for Mayor Victor D. Treviño, for JD Gonzalez, for Poncho Casso, and for Alyssa Cigarroa — hers in two parts. Between Gonzalez and Casso, the list prints a fifth name: Jorge A. Garza. His name is the only one of the five with no report attached — plain text where every other candidate's name opens a document. Webb Watch 956 checked every other 2026 section of the page as well: the July 15 and January 15 semiannual sections list current officeholders only, and Garza's name appears nowhere else on the page. As of October 23, 2026, there is no campaign finance report from Jorge A. Garza posted by the City Secretary — no cover sheet, no donor list, no spending record.

What that means voters cannot see

For the other four candidates, any voter can open the report and read the cover-sheet totals — how much the campaign raised, spent, and borrowed — and the itemized list of contributors behind them. For Garza, none of that exists in the public record. Who is financing his run for mayor, how much he has spent, whether he is funding the campaign himself, whether any political action committee has given to him — the record, as posted, answers none of it.

What it does not prove

A missing report is not, by itself, proof of wrongdoing, and the law offers explanations the public record cannot rule out. Texas allows an opposed candidate who declares, on his campaign treasurer appointment, that he will stay under a state-set threshold for contributions and expenditures to file under "modified reporting" — which exempts him from the 30-day and 8-day pre-election reports, though he must still account for the full cycle in a later semiannual or final report. A candidate running a very small campaign can fall under that rule. It is also possible for a paper report to have been delivered to the City Secretary and not yet posted. Only the City Secretary's Office can say whether anything was received, and only the Garza campaign can say which explanation applies. Webb Watch 956 is reporting what the public record shows: as of October 23, nothing is posted.

The next deadline

Garza is the least-known name in this race. He is officially on the ballot, but he was not among the four candidates listed for the Laredo Chamber of Commerce's October 7 mayoral forum, and little verifiable information about his platform is publicly available. The next filing deadline — the 8th-day report, covering September 25 through October 24 — arrives Monday, October 26, 2026. If reports appear under that deadline for the other candidates and Garza's name again stands alone with nothing attached, voters will go to the polls on November 3 knowing less about who stands behind his campaign than about any other name on the mayoral ballot. Webb Watch 956 will update this story if a report from the Garza campaign is posted.

Sources: City of Laredo, Campaign Finance Reports (City Secretary's Office) — https://www.cityoflaredo.com/departments/city-secretary-s-office/campaign-finance-reports ; City of Laredo, 2026 General Elections — https://www.cityoflaredo.com/departments/2026-general-elections ; Texas Ethics Commission, Candidate and Officeholder FAQ (modified reporting) — https://www.ethics.state.tx.us/resources/FAQs/FAQ_COH_Legal.php ; Texas Election Code, Title 15, Sections 254.181–254.183 ; VoteLaredo, 2026 Elections — https://votelaredo.com/

Garza's name is on the city's list — with nothing attached. Webb Watch 956 checked every 2026 section of the city's campaign finance page, and there is no report from him to follow.
title: Follow the Money: The Mayoral Candidate With No Report on File
